column1: Make a well in the flour, add the whole egg and 3 yolks, and mix with a fork, gradually drawing in the flour until a ball forms.
Knead on the counter for 10–15 minutes until smooth and springy. Wrap and rest for 20 minutes.
Pour boiling water over the spinach in a colander and let it cool. Squeeze out as much water as possible by hand and then in a clean towel, and chop finely.
Mix the spinach with the ricotta, Parmesan, garlic, lemon zest, and nutmeg. Season well and load into a piping bag with a 1–2cm nozzle.
Halve the dough and roll each piece through a pasta machine, passing it twice on each setting, down to the second-thinnest setting. Lay both sheets on a floured surface.
Pipe four 7cm rings of filling on one sheet, about 8cm apart, then pipe a second layer on top to form 2cm-high walls.
Gently drop an egg yolk into the middle of each ring.
Brush the pasta around the filling with water, lay the second sheet over the top, and press it around each mound to push out any air.
Cut out the ravioli with a 10cm round cutter and pinch the edges to seal well.
Lower the ravioli into a large pot of boiling salted water and cook for 3 minutes, then lift into two serving bowls.
Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the sage for 1–2 minutes until crisp.
Spoon the sage butter over the ravioli, top with extra Parmesan if you like, and serve at once.
